title: 5 Better Phones to Choose Over the Google Pixel 11 Pro – Digital Trends Picks
body:
Google’s latest flagship, the Pixel 11 Pro, has been praised for its refined camera system, clean Android experience, and solid build quality, but it arrives at a price point that leaves many consumers looking for alternatives. As competition in the premium smartphone market intensifies, several rivals now promise either superior performance, more versatile designs, or a better value proposition for the same budget. From a foldable that redefines multitasking to a mid‑range powerhouse that punches above its weight, these five devices are emerging as compelling substitutes for anyone hesitant to splurge on Google’s newest offering.

First on the list is Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 6, a device that shifts the conversation from incremental upgrades to a fundamentally different form factor. The Fold 6 retains the 7.6‑inch inner AMOLED display with a 120 Hz refresh rate, but Samsung has managed to shave weight and thickness, making the phone feel less like a tablet strapped to a handset. Its Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset delivers a noticeable edge in raw processing power, while the multitasking interface lets users run up to three apps side‑by‑side—a capability the Pixel 11 Pro’s single screen simply cannot match. For users who prioritize productivity on the go, the Fold 6 offers a compelling blend of portability and desktop‑class functionality, albeit at a premium price that still undercuts Google’s top‑tier model.

If a more conventional slab is preferred, the OnePlus 12 Pro stands out for delivering flagship performance at a comparatively modest cost. Equipped with the same Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor as Samsung’s foldable, the OnePlus 12 Pro pairs it with a 120 Hz LTPO display and a 5,000 mAh battery that easily lasts a full day of heavy use. The device’s OxygenOS skin continues to be lauded for its speed and minimal bloat, providing an experience that feels close to stock Android while adding useful customization options. Crucially, OnePlus has upped its camera game, offering a triple‑lens system with a 50 MP main sensor that rivals the Pixel’s computational photography, but at a price roughly $200 lower than the Pixel 11 Pro.

Apple’s iPhone 16 Pro also merits consideration, especially for users already entrenched in the iOS ecosystem. The A18 Bionic chip delivers industry‑leading efficiency, translating into smoother gaming, faster AI tasks, and longer battery life despite a smaller 3,200 mAh cell. Apple’s new periscope telephoto lens extends optical zoom to 6×, a feature the Pixel series still lacks. While the iPhone’s price remains high, trade‑in programs and carrier subsidies often bring the effective cost closer to Google’s flagship, making it a viable alternative for those who value ecosystem integration and long‑term software support.

For consumers who want a premium experience without breaking the bank, the Xiaomi 13 Ultra offers an impressive balance of specs and price. Its 1‑inch Sony IMX989 sensor, co‑engineered with Leica, delivers exceptional low‑light performance that competes directly with Google’s computational photography. Powered by Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 and a 120 Hz OLED panel, the phone feels swift and responsive. Xiaomi’s MIUI skin, while more feature‑rich than Android One, includes a suite of privacy controls that address many of the concerns users have with heavily customized Android skins. At a launch price roughly $150 less than the Pixel 11 Pro, the 13 Ultra presents a strong value case for photography enthusiasts.

Finally, the Motorola Edge 40 Pro rounds out the lineup as a device that blends design flair with solid performance. Its curved OLED display, 144 Hz refresh rate, and near‑stock Android experience make it a visually appealing and user‑friendly option. The phone’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor ensures it can handle demanding apps and games, while the inclusion of a 50 W fast‑charging solution means users spend less time tethered to a wall. Motorola’s commitment to providing regular security updates for three years adds a layer of confidence for buyers wary of rapid software obsolescence.

As the smartphone market continues to evolve, the Pixel 11 Pro’s strengths are increasingly matched—or even surpassed—by a diverse array of competitors. Whether it’s the innovative foldable design of Samsung’s Z Fold 6, the cost‑effective power of OnePlus, the ecosystem depth of Apple, the photographic prowess of Xiaomi, or the balanced appeal of Motorola, consumers now have a richer set of choices than ever before. Looking ahead, the pressure on Google to differentiate its flagship devices will only grow, prompting the company to push further in areas like AI integration, battery technology, and perhaps new form
